catalog.summary: File that belongs to a message or record.

patternAbsent.reason: There is no Authoring Practices pattern for a file shown inside a message, a record or a tray. The file's own target and its remove control follow the Button pattern and the native anchor; the set is a native list.

roles.root: listitem inside the group; no role when the attachment stands alone

group.focusable: tabindex=-1, so it can take focus when its last attachment is removed
group.reason: The set is a part of the one member, as `tag` holds its group. A second member would be a second reference page for a list with one axis, and the attachment inside it is the same object whether it stands in a set or alone.

vocabulary.reason: `upload` acquires and transfers files; this family shows a file that already belongs to something. They share the words for a file and nothing else.

kindsReason: The scale is `upload`'s, read under its own name. A shared name (`--slotted-file-kind-*`) would move twelve files across three families and the theme; it is a reopening if a third family needs the scale.

preview.image: an `img` with `alt=""`, `loading="lazy"` and `decoding="async"` when the page gives a source; the file name is already the attachment's name, and a list of many attachments fetches only the thumbnails in sight
preview.fallback: the kind's tile with the kind's mark knocked out of it
preview.error: an image that fails to load returns to the tile; the failure is internal state, not a state of the contract

trigger.stretch: a transparent `::after` on the trigger, inset over the root, so the whole attachment is the target and the accessible name stays the file name
trigger.blocked: a `button` takes the native `disabled`; an `a` takes `aria-disabled="true"` and the activation is refused, while `loading` or `disabled` holds
trigger.reason: Every surveyed implementation makes the whole file a target, and assistant-ui lets the page substitute the element. A name that is a real anchor keeps `href`, `download` and the modified click a browser gives a link.

actionsPlacement.reason: Interactive content may not nest inside `a` or `button`. `actions` is the trigger's container's sibling and sits above the stretched target, the decision `list-item` took for `content` and `actions`.

filename.reason: CSS cannot truncate in the middle, so `splitName` splits at the last dot and the stem shrinks while the extension stays. The whole name stays in the DOM and in the trigger's `title`, because truncation never removes content.

removal.keysBoundTo: the root, so the keys answer wherever focus is inside the attachment

focus.reason: Removing the focused attachment moves focus to the one that took its place, then to the last one, then to the group. `removal-focus` observes the DOM, so it is right however the consumer removed the file.

removal.reason: The list of attachments is the consumer's. Removal is a request with a reason and no value, so no controlled pair exists (`docs/state-and-events.md`).

progress.accessibleName: the file name, as the bar's hidden label
progress.reason: A tray that sends files on its own shows the transfer on the attachment it is sending. The bar is `progress-indicator`'s, drawn as the attachment's bottom edge, as `upload` draws it.

invalid.announcedBy: the trigger's `aria-describedby`, which names the detail and the message
invalid.reason: A color and a border say the file failed; the sentence in `message` says why, and a reader hears it on the file's own name.

loading.refuses: the trigger's activation; `remove` stays operable so a transfer can be abandoned

disabled.controls: the trigger, every family action and `remove` take the native `disabled` (a `button`) or `aria-disabled` (an `a`)

keyboard.effect: moves to the next focusable element; the trigger, each action and `remove` are in the page tab sequence
moves to the previous focusable element, under the same rule
follows a link trigger, activates a button trigger, an action or `remove`
keyboard.focus: stays on the control; after a removal, `removal-focus` moves it

keyboard.effect: activates a button trigger, an action or `remove`
asks to remove the attachment when it is removable, with the reason `keyboard`; a repeat is ignored
keyboard.focus: the next attachment, the previous one, or the group
the next attachment, the previous one, or the group

rovingReason: An attachment holds up to four targets and a set holds dozens; a composite widget with arrow keys would hide the actions behind a mode. The page tab sequence reaches every one, which is what `list-item` does for the same shape.

empty.reason: AI Elements ships `AttachmentEmpty`. A set with no attachments is the page's `result-state`, and an empty group draws nothing: `{files.length ? <AttachmentGroup>…</AttachmentGroup> : <ResultState … />}`.

hoverCard.reason: AI Elements ships a hover card. `hover-card` composes around the trigger: `<HoverCard><HoverCardTrigger render={(props) => <AttachmentTrigger {...props} />} />…</HoverCard>`.

fade.reason: ReUI fades the ends of a scrolling strip. `scroll-area` holds the reopening for a veil driven by `animation-timeline: scroll()`; a strip inside a ScrollArea receives it.

processing.reason: ReUI draws `processing` with an infinite shimmer. A file the server is still working on is `loading` without a value, and the indeterminate bar stops under reduced motion where a shimmer did not.

messagesReason: The remove control's name is one message with the file name in it, `Remove claim-form.pdf`, so a language that puts the file first writes its own order; it and the tile's word for a file without an extension come from the catalog of the language in force, laid over by the attachment's `messages`.
